 Low Pressure System Threatens Coastal Flooding, Rip Currents
 Second low could gain subtropical traits while moving near mid-Atlantic coast
 Published:  November 20, 2026 at 3:48 PM Tags:  Weather , Tropics . (.) Gale Warnings continue for a non-tropical low pressure system over east central Florida and along a trough extending northward along the Florida coast toward the Carolinas.
 Associated seas are 8 to 12 ft, reaching as high as 16 ft in the waters of strongest winds off the northern Bahamas.
 There are several broad areas of low pressure located along a front that extends from central Florida eastward into the Atlantic for several hundred miles and are producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms.
 . (.) One of the low pressure areas, near the central Florida coast, is likely to remain inland without significant development.
 A second low farther east could acquire subtropical or tropical characteristics while it moves generally northward to north-northeastward, passing near or east of the mid-Atlantic coast through the weekend.
 Regardless of subtropical or tropical development, this large weather system will produce gusty winds, dangerous surf, rip currents and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week.
 The threat of flash flooding will continue across portions of the northeast Florida peninsula today, spreading northward over coastal portions of the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic over the weekend. 
 The formation chance through 48 hours remains at 30 percent, while the formation chance through 7 days drops to 40 percent.
